text: The three Epic 2 packages RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH and BOOKING_MATCH are the rule fixture set through which the notice path of rwb-comms is proved, resolved by package code, rule ID and version through the contract of RWB-P3-E2042-CON with their labels and counts of 16 November 2026; no fourth package is read and no notice is attached to a package by assumption.
why: The legacy story attaches no notice to any of the three packages, the P6 module specification names no package, and RWB-P6-E1073-APP records the same hole; the notice path has to be proved against something, so the legacy values are used and the assignment is left open.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-042 section 2 and section 8; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1.2; TSD P6 Communications v2 T2; P6 context pack ownership rows; RWB-P6-E1073-APP precondition 6
confirm: The rule registry owner and the rwb-comms tech lead settle which package the service is assigned and whether any notice reads it, before the integration stage.
impact: AC1 and AC5 are proved against the legacy values and stay valid whatever the assignment; a service assigned to another package runs the same tests with that package's code and its own label.

text: The consumption of rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1 stays with RWB-P6-E1073-APP and feeds the local copy only; the notice path of this story consumes no event, adds no listener and reacts to no package state, so a load, an approval, a promotion or a rollback raises nothing on it.
why: Architecture v5 slide 13 gives P6 to P7 a Temporal cell and no event cell, while the published contract and the local-copy story require the subscription; the notice path is written so that it holds under either reading.
read: Arch v5 slide 13 matrix and notes; RWB-P3-E2042-CON AC4; RWB-P6-E1073-APP preconditions and flow steps 3 and 4
confirm: The solution architect confirms the P6 to P7 cell of the connection matrix and the owner of the local copy confirms that no notice-path class subscribes.
impact: A promotion reaches the decisions taken after it through the local copy and never through a notice-path listener; the architecture test blocks any second consumer.

text: The package code, the version label and the checksum of a notice decision are recorded on the decision_log_entry row written through the library of DP-03 in the same transaction as the notice and its outbox row; rwb_comms gains no table and no column, and notice, template and merge_field keep the fields of TSD P6 v2 T3.1.
why: The legacy story adds no field to any table, the notice table has no rule-version column and no source states where the pin lives; a new column would be invented, and the decision record is the place the target design already keeps the rule version.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-042 section 11 and section 12; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1; DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03
confirm: The decision-record owner confirms the two field IDs that carry the package code and the checksum when the record is published, and the data steward confirms that no notice column is needed.
impact: Audit reads the version from the record and never from the notice; a reader of a notice answer sees no rule field, and a change of the record shape does not move the notice tables.

text: The eleven dependency rows the DP table adds — H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON — are carried in the pattern application only, and the metadata rows keep Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P3-E2042-CON as the Work Package fixes them.
why: The pattern table and the plan disagree and the plan's rows are fixed by the Work Package; every added row is a wave-0 platform contract or a published contract built against as a fake, so none blocks the build.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R5.7 rule 8; Work Package story row for RWB-P6-E2042-APP
confirm: The tech lead confirms that the platform contracts are prerequisites of the wave-0 train and that no added row is a build block for this lane.
impact: The story stays Day 1; a missing platform contract delays the wave-0 train and not this lane, and no lane depth is added.

text: When no package version is in force a notice request is refused: NoPackageInForce is answered, no notice row is created, nothing is dispatched and the caller sees MSG-GEN-006; no hold reason and no notice state are added by this story.
why: No source states the resting state or the message of a request without a rule version in force, and the only hold reason given by the module specification is TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN.
read: FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1.4.2 and A2.1.4.3; TSD P6 Communications v2 T4; RWB-P3-E2042-CON AC5
confirm: The business analyst and the owner of the notice states confirm the refusal, and the message owner confirms that MSG-GEN-006 carries the empty-version case.
impact: A request made while no version is in force creates no notice and no dispatch item; a caller retries after the registry is fixed and receives one notice, never two.

text: The three route-set fields are read and copied verbatim only where a notice is decided by a route-set rule, and the case next action, its owner and its due date stay with RWB-E2-035 and its rwb-case story; the legacy values of R-RES-04 are the fixture.
why: The legacy criterion proves the route set through the case engine, and no source of the P6 module attaches a route-set row to a notice; carrying the behaviour whole would move RWB-E2-035 into this service.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-042 AC5 and BR4; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1; P6 context pack ownership rows
confirm: The business analyst and the owner of RWB-E2-035 confirm the boundary between a notice next action and a case next action before the first release.
impact: A notice decided by a route-set rule shows the three values and names the rule and version; a case next action is set only by the case engine and never by a notice.
